self_statements.quote: Ready to dig into the styling issue when you are. I'm thinking we'll want to look at network requests to see if CSS resources are failing to load through the vite proxy, or if something about the X-Frame-Options/CSP stripping is affecting stylesheet delivery.
self_statements.context: magent theorizing about styling problem before actually investigating

self_statements.quote: There's the problem. Look at the network requests: [GET] https://justin0.hunter.cryptograss.live/load.php?... => [404]. The iframe loads via `/piki` which gets proxied to [REDACTED].xyz. But MediaWiki's CSS/JS resources use relative paths like `/load.php?...`
self_statements.context: magent identifying the actual root cause of styling issue after investigating network requests

self_statements.quote: That's the fix. All network requests returning 200 now. The PickiPedia iframe is now fully styled - search box, navigation, the green MusicianInfo infobox, proper MediaWiki layout. **The problem was**: MediaWiki resources (`load.php`, `api.php`, `index.php`) use absolute paths from root. When embedded in an iframe, these resolved to the rabbithole host instead of [REDACTED].xyz.
self_statements.context: magent explaining what was broken and how it was fixed

philosophy.summary: Discussion of IPFS deduplication: same CID stored once regardless of how many pins reference it. Distinction between 'pinning redundantly' (multiple entries) vs 'storing redundantly' (actual disk usage).
philosophy.quote: If they do match (which you're saying they do), then IPFS deduplicates at the block level - you're only storing the data once, just pinning it twice (once as standalone, once as part of the directory structure)

philosophy.summary: PickiPedia 'Is Not WikiPedia' - the farcical content isn't a bug to be fixed but a feature to be preserved. 'Keep the structured data tight' is the actual requirement.
philosophy.quote: OK so tell you what, let's revert that edit and see if we can together find the vibe more... The page is kinda pleasantly broken / farcical, and that's exactly the kind of content that makes [REDACTED] fun. Just keep the structured data tight and we'll be good.
